text:
marta: Heads-up — customer acme-app reported a sudden spike on their March invoice. Their per-session dashboard shows token counts doubled for a set of short-lived sessions around 2026-03-10T14:02Z after a mobile network flap. Can we triage?

kevin: Which invoice / customer id? any repro steps or logs?

billing: invoice: https://billing.internal/acme/INV-2026-03-1023 (internal link), cust_id=acme-7b2. Billing shows ~+48k tokens vs dashboard over that hour. Filed as INC-5542.

marta: quick logs from gateway near the incident (redacted):
```
[14:02:11] ingress: conn-reset, session=abc123, trace=trc-01
[14:02:12] request received: req_id=R1, idempotency_key=mobile:tmp:xyz123, tokens=750
[14:02:12] routed -> host-7
[14:02:15] host-7 ack
---
[14:02:18] new connection from same device, session=abc123
[14:02:18] request received: req_id=R2, idempotency_key=mobile:tmp:xyz124, tokens=750
[14:02:18] routed -> host-9
[14:02:20] host-9 ack
```
Both R1 and R2 were accepted and surfaced to metering. Notes: idempotency_key differs (sdk created ephemeral per-conn).

eli: this matches an old mobile SDK behavior: on reconnect we generate a fresh ephemeral idempotency token. If a previous request actually went through but client didn't see the ack (conn reset), it retries with a different key -> server treats as new. Gateway retry/backoff could also resubmit.

kevin: can you repro quickly? steps to repro locally?

marta: repro steps I used in emulator:
1) start request with client network blocked after sending headers
2) simulate server ACK delayed (or host ack but client never reads)
3) client reconnects -> new idempotency token created -> send same payload -> get a second successful response
I attached a tiny script we used to simulate:
```
# simulate: send, drop tcp, reopen, resend
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: mobile:tmp:$RAND" -d @payload.json $API
# then immediately open new connection and send different Idempotency-Key but same payload
```

support-bot: /create-case INC-5542 linked to billing, assigned to kevin, eli, billing.

billing: provisional credit planned: refund duplication window for acme-7b2 while we confirm root cause.

sre-ops: short-term mitigation idea: gateway dedupe cache keyed by (customer_id + payload_hash) for 30s to collapse near-duplicate submissions coming from same session/ip. Longer-term: require persistent idempotency token in SDK or persist across reconnects.

eli: agree. Also recommend we increase idempotency TTL in ingress to 60s (current ephemeral TTL 10s) and add optional last-seen request fingerprint dedupe. Patch proposal in PR #4321.

kevin: I'll reproduce, add automated test in our e2e harness, and verify metering emits single usage record when dedupe enabled. ETA EOD. tagging @eli to review gateway patch. :eyes:

marta: thanks — billing will hold off final invoice adjustments until kevin confirms. please drop the repro output here when you have it.

kevin: quick repro results: with SDK ephemeral key behavior we see two distinct usage records in metering stream:
```
usage_record: cust=acme-7b2 session=abc123 request=R1 tokens=750 trace=trc-01
usage_record: cust=acme-7b2 session=abc123 request=R2 tokens=750 trace=trc-02
```
With gateway dedupe feature toggled on (local flag), duplicates collapsed to one record.

billing: noted. Issued provisional refund for duplicated 750 tokens x occurrences. Sending customer note.

marta: action items
- kevin: land e2e test + gateway dedupe PR (#4321) — owner kevin — ETA 2026-03-11
- eli: update mobile SDK guidance to persist idempotency across reconnects + runtime change note — ETA 2026-03-17
- billing: finalize refund after kevin confirms in prod — owner billing — pending
- support: inform customer and provide workaround (toggle to server-side dedupe) — owner marta

kevin: assigned, will follow up in INC-5542. :white_check_mark:
